key_insight: HVAF spraying can produce thick NiTi coatings that retain martensitic transformation and functional shape-memory behavior, but only after heat treatment to overcome spray-induced defects and inhomogeneity.
engineering_relevance: This work shows a practical route to add smart, self-actuating NiTi surfaces on steel components for wear and thermal-function applications where conventional ceramic coatings may be less suitable.
method: HVAF-sprayed NiTi coatings onto mild steel using four parameter sets
Characterized composition, porosity, microstructure, phase transformation, and thermomechanical response
Evaluated functionality with annealing, 3-point bending, nanoindentation, and scratch tests
evidence_signal: The coatings were 100–300 µm thick and showed martensitic transformation plus thermal actuation and shape memory effects, despite high defect density and internal stress.
watch_item: As-sprayed coatings are not fully functional and need annealing; their inhomogeneous microstructure and limited tensile strength may constrain reliability in demanding service conditions.
paper_title: HVAF Spraying of NiTi Coatings: Microstructure, Phase Transformation and Shape Memory Behavior
